Welcome to Ecuador!

Arrival in Quito, the capital of Ecuador.

Our team will meet you at the international airport and help you with your transfer to the hotel. The drive takes about an hour and offers panoramic views of the Andean landscape on the way into the city. You will stay at the four-star Rio Amazonas, a comfortable, modern hotel and a convenient base for exploring Quito.

In the evening, join your guide for an included dinner to go over the tour details and ask any questions.

31 December 2026. Quito, the equator and New Year

After breakfast at the hotel, set out on a sightseeing tour of Quito. The tour takes in panoramic views, historic churches and ornate rooftops and introduces the colonial art and architecture of the capital. Quito was founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city and lies at an altitude of 2,850 metres. Its historic centre preserves landmarks of colonial architecture, with elaborate buildings and richly decorated interiors that showcase the Quito school of sculpture and its blend of Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous influences. Spend four hours in the Old Town and see why Quito's historic centre was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. In the afternoon, visit Ciudad Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum. Ciudad Mitad del Mundo brings together tourism, culture and science. Its Equator Monument marks the middle of the Earth at 0 degrees latitude. Surrounded by colonial-style architecture and striking scenery, it offers a chance to learn about Ecuador's geography. The monument is topped with a metal globe representing the Earth. The Intiñan Museum has promoted Ecuadorian culture since 1960. Its interactive exhibits show how the Incas determined the location of the equator and include hands-on experiments such as balancing an egg on a nail. You can try the demonstrations and learn about Ecuadorian culture. After the visits, return to the four-star Rio Amazonas,

where you can relax after your day in Quito. (Meals: breakfast)

Stops: Basilica of the National Vow, the main square, the Golden Church, San Francisco Square, the hill with the Virgin Mary, the Intiñan Museum and Mitad del Mundo.

New Year celebrations:

After the tour, take a short guided walk through the tourist district to see Ecuadorian New Year traditions, including the effigies of the old year that are burned at midnight and the widows who mourn its passing.

Cities throughout Ecuador mark the New Year by burning an effigy of the departing year. The idea is to leave the year's troubles behind in the flames and welcome the new year in the hope that it will be better.

People make the effigy from old clothes and cardboard or paper and stuff it with straw or sawdust, often adding fireworks. It is burned at midnight on 31 December.

The effigy is accompanied in its final minutes by grieving widows. Ecuadorian men dressed in women's clothes play these roles, dancing in the street and asking passers-by for small change for the old year's funeral.

Burning the old year on 31 December is a cleansing ritual meant to drive away bad energy and welcome the new year.

Return to the hotel for free time, followed by a New Year's dinner with traditional music and dancing. Your guide will let you know the dinner schedule.
